plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs light up the cold season with rose-like blooms of layered, satin petals around golden stamens. They stand out against deep green leaves in winter gardens and woodlands.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, with flowering from about December through April and a strong peak from January to March
plants.location: Coastal and southern Japan, including Kyushu, Shikoku and the Pacific coast of Honshu
plants.funFact: In Japan the camellia, called tsubaki, is a classic tea-garden flower. Its seeds are pressed into prized camellia oil, traditionally used for hair care and for polishing blades.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall, slender stems hold rounded clusters of trumpet-shaped blue flowers above arching, strap-like leaves. In midsummer they ripple along sunny borders and roadsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, roughly December to February
plants.location: Eastern coastal South Africa, widely grown in Australia and New Zealand gardens
plants.funFact: Despite the common name, it is not a true lily. Its name comes from Greek words meaning 'love flower', and its thick, fleshy roots store water through dry spells.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Bare branches burst into fragrant, five-petaled blossoms while winter still holds on. The sweet, spicy scent drifts through cold air, and early varieties open in the mildest parts of the country.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to early spring, with early varieties opening from January in milder regions
plants.location: Warmer parts of Japan, such as the Izu Peninsula and the Pacific coast, and southern China
plants.funFact: Ume blooms before cherry blossoms and is seen as a herald of spring in East Asian culture. Its fruits are pickled into umeboshi and steeped into plum wine.
